header: L6 · The test architect who has seen coverage lie · sonnet
verdict: Close: R11-05 (I17 daemon-head and ignored-file cases) reads as resolved; the import-closure test still names no red fixture, and the test requirements 12.4 states for the pr job are not in T005 acceptance.

findings.defect: The import-closure test is held by 'a test' with no red fixture, no -test flag, no stdlib rule (first path element has no dot), and no mutation row; R11-01's resolution moved these to T005 but they did not arrive.
findings.scenario: The implementer filters on a prefix that also matches a third-party path, or skips test imports; a dependency enters the pr package and the test stays green.
findings.change: Add to T005 requirement (b): a fixture package importing a path outside the approvals globs makes the test red; the test runs go list -deps -test; the stdlib rule is a first path element without a dot; removing the glob check turns the fixture red.

findings.section: 12 12.4 (check-name collision, head pr-job event, ## escape); plan T005 acceptance
findings.defect: 12.4 now requires fixtures for: a head job whose check name equals the pr job's, a head version of the pr job file naming another event, and the escape cases (leading space, U+00A0, ##[ ); T005 acceptance (all lines are fixtures) lists none of them, nor the hostile-git fixture.
findings.scenario: T005 merges with every listed acceptance line green and the name-collision refusal absent; no named test turns red.
findings.change: List these fixtures as T005 acceptance lines, each with the removal that turns it red.

findings.defect: The new test that the mise.toml gh is not below the 12.1 floor says 'with a fixture' but names no pair (a below-floor pin fails, an at-floor pin passes), and no task in the plan owns it.
findings.scenario: The floor is read from 12.1 prose by a loose regex; a reworded floor leaves the test green on a stale number.
findings.change: Name the two fixtures and the plan task that builds the test; state that it fails when 12.1 holds no parseable floor.
